cases.notes:

items.title: TraderTraitor (DPRK)
items.body:
aliases: Lazarus-linked unit
Attributed by FBI, TRM Labs, Chainalysis.
Also behind the $1.5B Bybit hack (2025).

items.title: Pyongyang, DPRK — attributed origin
items.body: State-sponsored; proceeds reported to fund weapons programmes.

items.title: Attribution assessments
items.body:
TRM Labs: linked to North Korean hackers.
Chainalysis (Levin): likely TraderTraitor, citing links to earlier attacks.
Elliptic: almost certainly the largest known theft of any kind.
FBI alert 31 Oct: North Korea responsible.

items.title: Related incidents — same playbook
items.body:
Bybit, $1.5B (Feb 2025) — FBI: TraderTraitor.
KelpDAO (Apr 2026).
Binance: features of this attack match both.

items.title: Spearphishing via Service
items.body: Fake job interviews used to reach engineers (Binance statement).

items.title: FBI attributes the attack to DPRK
items.body: Publishes ETH, BTC and SOL addresses tied to the theft; asks the public for information. Same day Binance reports 90% of losses replenished.

items.title: FBI Cyber alert — North Korea responsible
items.body: Source of the published attacker addresses.

items.title: Intrusion campaign begins
items.body: June 2026 (day not published). Multi-stage: employee devices, internal development systems, wallet infrastructure. The platform's own AI tool was reportedly leveraged.

items.title: Status of the funds
items.body:
Binance, 3 Nov: ~$2.85B frozen or intercepted (≈45% of $6.34B).
Press summary: ~$3.0B frozen by issuers and partners · ~$1.5B could not be frozen · ~$1.8B still with the attackers.
No conversion to fiat observed as of 30 Oct.

items.title: Binance preliminary report; DPRK denial
items.body: $2.85B frozen/intercepted; 98% of stolen tokens replenished. Kim Yo Jong (KCNA) denies North Korean involvement, also for Bybit. US Secret Service tracking and freezing funds.

items.title: Withdrawals resume
items.body: $4.65B processed on day one, starting with ETH, USDT, USDC. Losses covered from SAFU, futures insurance fund, BTC reserve and treasury.
Initial statement: entry via a compromised software engineer's laptop. Later: other issues found. Attack prepared at least 36 hours in advance.

items.title: Issuers freeze stablecoins
items.body: Tether freezes wallets 17:01 ET, Circle 17:04. Tether blocks the Binance hot wallet 18:06, Circle 19:53. Binance revokes the attackers' permissions 20:10 ET. Ripple also freezes.
Losses by chain: ETH $3.8B · BTC $1.5B (18,270 BTC) · TRON $628M · XRP $296M · SOL $96M. Ten chains in total.

items.title: CNBC — what we know and what comes next
items.body: $6.36B moved across 10 blockchains, most within ~20 minutes.

items.title: User Execution
items.body: Malicious software delivered through the interview lure; engineer device compromised.

items.title: Hot wallets drained — 16:05 ET
items.body: Starts on XRP Ledger 16:05 ET; Ethereum and Bitcoin 16:20. Main ETH transaction 16:24 (64 transfers); one transfer above $2.5B. ~20 minutes, ten chains.

items.title: Second wave — Avalanche, Polygon
items.body: 19:05 ET. Final Ethereum transaction 19:56 ET.

items.title: Wikipedia — 2026 Binance hack
items.body: Running summary with per-chain losses and the freeze timeline.

items.title: Attack path — EIP-7702
items.body: Hot wallet drained via EIP-7702 account delegation (CEO Richard Teng). Signatures obtained in advance, executed in one burst. Full post-mortem pending.

items.title: Financial Theft
items.body: $6.3B across ten chains.

items.title: 17,260 ETH moved to a fresh wallet
items.body: 01:15 ET. First visible laundering step; funds not yet converted to fiat.

items.title: Richard Teng — Binance CEO
items.body: Public statements: EIP-7702 used on the hot wallet; $6B set aside; services to resume within 40 hours.
Pattern match with Bybit and KelpDAO: small Tornado Cash withdrawals fund an operator wallet; staging long before the theft; pre-signed, one burst.

items.title: Largest single transfer of the drain
items.body: Part of the 64-transfer Ethereum batch at 16:24 ET.

items.title: First laundering hop
items.body: 01:15 ET, 30 Oct. Paste the published address and tx hash here.
Open the FBI alert, copy the published ETH / BTC / SOL addresses, then run Extract IOCs to pin them as wallet indicators.

items.title: Guardian — withdrawals resume after record hack
Attacker wallet (from the FBI alert)
items.body: Paste one published address per card, or use Extract IOCs.

items.title: Okta look-alike login domain
items.body: Spoofed SSO portal; registered via privacy proxy. Pivot on registrar + cert.
Check whether SMS fallback is still enabled for admins

items.title: TraderTraitor
items.body:
aka Jade Sleet, UNC4899, Slow Pisces
DPRK · crypto theft

Targets exchanges and Web3 developers with fake job offers and trojanised coding tasks, then drains hot wallets in one burst. Attributed by the FBI to the Bybit (2025) and Binance (2026) heists.

judgement.text: We assess with moderate confidence that a financially motivated English-speaking crew is running a vendor-themed Okta/ServiceNow vishing campaign against e-commerce SaaS providers.
judgement.dissent: A state actor using the same kit cannot be excluded until victimology is wider than e-commerce.
